h1: Loyalty programmes for brewpubs and what they really return
title: Brewpub Loyalty Programmes That Pay Back | Craft Beer School
desc: How brewpub loyalty programmes in India work, what they cost in margin and how to tell whether yours brings guests back or just gives away beer.
teaser: Ten stamps and the eleventh pint is free. Simple to run. Quite easy to lose money on.
standfirst: A loyalty programme is a discount with a memory. Run well, it brings regulars back on quiet nights. Run badly, it gives free beer to people who were coming anyway. Here is how to tell the difference.
sections: What a loyalty programme is really buying

Every reward is paid for out of margin. The only question is whether it changes behaviour. If a guest visits more often, brings friends or comes on a Tuesday instead of a Saturday, the reward has bought something. If they would have come anyway, you have simply cut your price for your best customers.

That sounds obvious. It is also the trap most programmes fall into, because the people who collect stamps fastest are your existing regulars.

• Stamp or visit cards. Buy a set number, get one free. Cheap to run, easy to understand, easy to fake.
  • Points on spend. A percentage of each bill comes back as credit. Usually run through your POS or a loyalty app.
  • Membership or mug clubs. A paid membership that brings perks such as a larger pour, early access to releases or member nights.
  • Tiered rewards. Status levels that add perks as spend grows. Powerful but complicated for a single outlet.

Food rewards are often easier than beer rewards in India. Some state excise rules restrict free drinks, discounts or promotions on alcohol. Liquor advertising is tightly limited. Check your state's current position before you print anything that promises a free pint.

Work out the cost of the reward at cost price, not menu price. A free starter costs you its food cost, not its price. A free beer costs you the beer, the duty already paid and the glass washing. Then estimate how many rewards will be redeemed in a month.

A worked example: say a pint sells for ₹400 and costs ₹110 in beer and duty. A ten-stamp card that gives the eleventh pint free looks like a 9 percent discount at menu prices. In cash terms the free pint costs ₹110 against the ₹2,900 of gross profit the ten paid pints earned, a little under 4 percent. Your own numbers will differ. Our taproom economics guide shows how to find them.

A programme you cannot measure is a programme you cannot defend. Link it to your POS so each member has an ID and each visit is recorded. Then watch three things over a few months:

  1. Visit frequency of members against similar guests who did not join.
  2. Share of member visits on quiet days.
  3. Average bill per member visit.

If members visit no more often than before, the programme is a discount. Our guide to POS and inventory software for brewpubs covers which systems handle loyalty well.
Rewards that cost little and mean a lot

The best rewards are often not discounts at all. A first taste of a new batch from the bright tank. A seat at a brewer's tasting. Their name on a mug behind the bar. A members' night where the head brewer explains why the hazy IPA changed. These cost very little in cash and build the sense of belonging that keeps people coming back. They also avoid most excise questions about free alcohol.

Always offer something good for guests who do not drink: food, alcohol-free beer, merchandise. A programme that rewards only volume of beer sends the wrong message and some states will not allow it.

A digital programme collects phone numbers, emails and visit histories. That is personal data. India's data protection rules expect businesses to collect it for a stated purpose with consent and to keep it safe. Ask members clearly what you will send them and how often. Do not share the list with partners or sell it. Choose a loyalty or POS provider that explains where data is stored and who can see it.

Use the data well and members will thank you. A message when their favourite style is back on tap is welcome. Three promotional messages a week is how members unsubscribe.

Give any programme a fixed review date. If the numbers show it is not changing behaviour, close it politely and put the budget into events or community nights instead. A loyalty card nobody uses is also a reminder at the till that you tried something and it did not work. Tidy endings matter.

Loyalty is one tool in a wider kit for building a regular crowd: events, social media, collaborations and a taproom people want to sit in. Choosing between them is easier with a plan.
faqs: Can a brewpub in India give free beer as a loyalty reward?
Some states restrict free drinks, discounts or promotions on alcohol. Check your state's current excise rules before offering beer rewards. Food and merchandise rewards are usually simpler.
A paid membership where regulars get perks such as a larger pour in their own mug, early access to releases or member events.
How do I know if my loyalty programme works?
Compare visit frequency and spend of members against similar guests who did not join. If members visit no more often, the programme is a discount rather than a driver.
